question: In the early 1980s, an aspartic acid-containing dipeptide sweetener was discovered, that was about 2000 times sweeter than sucrose. What is the name of that sweetener?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Alitame__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alitame is an aspartic acid-containing dipeptide sweetener**.
 
• It was developed by** Pfizer.**
 
• Currently marketed in some countries under the **brand name Aclame**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saccharin** is an **artificial sweetener.**
 
• **Aspartame** is an artificial **non-saccharide sweetener**.
 
• **Sucralose** is an **artificial sweetener** and **sugar substitute**.
